result.thesis: Kavach (train-protection) orders from ICF (~Rs675cr incl GST since May 2026) are turning into reported revenue and profit at a scale that is 8x last year, with CARE upgrading the rating to BBB. The earnings inflection is real in the filed numbers. But FY26 operating cash flow was negative (CFO/PAT -1.1), receivables are 268 days, Rs222cr of FY26 profit sits in inventory/WIP, and one quarter does not make a trend. Wide outcome range; the bear case is a cash-conversion failure. Needs Q2 collections before any size.

bear.assumptions: ASSUMPTION: Q1 FY27 was a lumpy billing quarter; FY27-28 PAT ~Rs200cr (EPS ~120); receivables (268 days) and WIP do not convert to cash, working-capital stress, CARE BBB limits tight, market de-rates to 6x.

base.assumptions: ASSUMPTION: Kavach order flow (~Rs675cr incl GST since May 2026) converts through FY28 at ~25-30% EBITDA margin; FY28 PAT ~Rs320cr; P/E 11x for a BBB, receivable-heavy railway-electronics vendor.

bull.assumptions: ASSUMPTION: order inflow keeps pace (Kavach rollout on EMU/trainsets), margins hold ~30%, collections normalise; FY28 PAT ~Rs500cr; 14x.

extreme_bull.assumptions: ASSUMPTION: large Kavach roll-out across zonal railways, PAT ~Rs670cr, 16x.
